title: Fine orbit coverage of generalized butterflies
summary: Decide whether the source's natural left-right linear-equivalence orbit of generalized butterflies covers every relevant permutation-equivalent biprojective function.

formal_statement.body: With $q=2^k$, $L=\mathbb F_{2^\ell}$ and the source-defined family $\mathcal B_{q,L}\subseteq\Pi_1\times\Pi_1$, let $\approx_L$ be equivalence under the natural left and right $\mathrm{GL}(2,L)$ actions. Prove that every source-relevant $F\in\Pi_1\times\Pi_1$ that is CCZ-equivalent to a permutation satisfies $F\approx_L B$ for some $B\in\mathcal B_{q,L}$, or exhibit a qualifying function outside this finer orbit.

scope.domain: Fine equivalence classes of generalized-butterfly and biprojective cryptographic functions
assumptions: $q$, $L$, $\Pi_1$, and $\mathcal B_{q,L}$ use the source definitions
The target is a source-relevant member of $\Pi_1\times\Pi_1$ and is CCZ-equivalent to a permutation
$\approx_L$ is the source's natural left-right $\mathrm{GL}(2,L)$ equivalence
scope.unresolved_remainder: The source resolves only a smaller right-action-plus-scaling count. Later closed-butterfly classifications do not establish $\approx_L$ coverage of the complete target subset of $\Pi_1\times\Pi_1$, so the finer universal coverage question remains open.

progress.summary: Remark 20 separately asks whether the finer $\approx_L$ class of generalized butterflies covers all relevant permutation-equivalent functions in $\Pi_1\times\Pi_1$.
